articles.text: Preparations for the new season are in full swing, and Basketball Sphere is set to deliver the most comprehensive EuroLeague Fantasy coverage throughout the entire 2026/27 campaign. Our goal is to provide you with all the data and insights needed to build a championship-caliber team and make smart decisions round after round. We will systematically cover every critical angle for your draft and weekly lineups. Through these deep dives, you will gain key insights into coaching tactics and rotation roles – the crucial factors that drive Fantasy output. The EuroLeague is about to begin, and so is our favorite game, EuroLeague Fantasy. If you want to stay one step ahead of the competition, it’s not enough to simply pick the best players. Good results often come down to the details and players flying under the radar whom others fail to identify in time. That’s why we’ve put together 10 fantasy tips that could take your game to the next level. EuroLeague Fantasy Basketball Sphere Competiton: JOIN the Challenge and Win Prizes 1. Pick players for multiple rounds Analyzing fixture difficulty is critical for long-term fantasy success . Before acquiring a player, evaluate their team’s upcoming schedule over the next three to four rounds. Identifying a target with a favorable sequence of games creates a durable asset for your roster. This forward-looking approach minimizes the need for frequent transfers, preserving flexibility for future rounds. Consequently, you can conserve valuable trade resources and concentrate on optimizing weaker positions across the rest of your squad. Plan ahead to build a stable lineup and maximize total fantasy production. 2. Don’t save credits on coaches Invest heavily in your head coach rather than saving credits. Premium options around 10 credits offer exceptional value, frequently securing a dependable 20 points when facing favorable matchups. Replicating that production with a 10-credit player is extremely rare. Apply schedule analysis to coaches just as you would with players. A premium coach with a soft stretch of games over multiple rounds serves as a stable scoring anchor. Keeping a reliable coach long term eliminates unnecessary transfers, allowing you to reallocate those valuable trade resources toward upgrading other positions across your roster. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: The Best Rookies 3. Have a backup captain for the second day Selecting your captain is a critical decision, as their performance earns double points. Design your roster with two premium captain options split across the schedule: one competing on the first day and another on the second. If your initial captain delivers a disappointing score, having a top-tier alternative on day two provides vital insurance. This setup allows you to switch the armband and take a second shot at high output. Structuring your squad around split-day captains mitigates risk and ensures a dependable fallback to maximize your total round score. 4. Have a backup center for the second day The center position in EuroLeague Fantasy is unique because we can select only two centers, unlike guards and forwards, where we choose four players. Centers very often produce the highest number of fantasy points. The advice is to try to have one center playing on the first day and another on the second day, as the second day center gives us another chance to make up for a poor performance, just like with the captain. If we have to use both centers on the first day, our advice is to use the two-center formation, because it can happen that a cheaper center scores more points than the more expensive one . In that case, we would have no opportunity to make a substitution between the first and second day. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Will Have Smaller Roles Compared to Their Previous Teams 5. Pick players from weaker teams Targeting standout performers from bottom-tier teams separates elite fantasy managers from average ones. Most competitors overlook these rosters entirely, yet key players on weaker squads carry high usage rates and generate massive fantasy output. Avoid deploying them against elite defensive teams. Instead, target them when bottom-table sides face off in competitive, high-possession matchups. In these balanced contests, first options on weaker teams shoulder the entire offensive load, transforming into high-value, must-have assets. Exploiting these lower-profile fixtures provides a distinct competitive edge and unlocks massive scoring potential for your roster. 6. Focus on making profit at the start Prioritize team value accumulation over short-term point tallies during the opening weeks. Your main objective across the first 10 rounds is expanding your credit budget by targeting undervalued assets capable of far exceeding their price tags. Building a high-value roster early yields massive long-term dividends. A inflated credit pool provides maximum flexibility, allowing you to easily afford premium superstars and elite options later in the season. Focus on roster appreciation early to set a strong financial foundation, expanding your budget and unlocking far greater flexibility for the rest of the campaign. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Produce Well but Aren’t Fantasy Options 7. Avoid players priced between 4.2 and 5.0 credits This is a tip that does not necessarily have to apply all the time, but it is particularly relevant at the very start of the season. We believe players in this price range should generally be avoided because they usually have very limited minutes, which means they don’t have enough time to produce a solid fantasy performance. This can lead to small losses in team value, which can add up significantly if the same mistake is repeated round after round. If a serious fantasy option appears in this price range, of course he should be considered, but our advice at the beginning is to go for 4.0-credit players instead. They cannot decrease our team value, and they might even make us some credits. There are a few interesting 4.0-credit options this season. 8. Avoid players from low-scoring games Another rule that many fantasy players overlook is the expected scoring level of a game. Players from teams that traditionally play at a high pace and score a lot of points are excellent fantasy options, and above all, so are their opponents. On the other hand, tougher teams that play in low-scoring games are worth avoiding, because fewer points in a game generally means fewer fantasy points for the players involved, and vice versa: more points in a game usually means more fantasy points for the players in that game. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Veterans Who Can Still Be Leaders 9. Follow the injury report Monitoring injury reports is essential for uncovering high-value fantasy opportunities. When a key player is sidelined, their absence frees up substantial court time and usage for remaining teammates. A backup center, guard, or forward stepping into a starting role instantly becomes a potent target. Combine roster shortages with favorable matchups. If an elevated backup faces an opponent that struggles to defend their position, they transform into a mandatory pick. Tracking injuries allows you to capitalize on temporary usage spikes, secure premium production at lower costs, and gain a decisive edge over managers who react too late. 10. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Centers
articles.text: It's the start of the 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] season, and everyone starts from scratch. You have just as much chance to win the grand prize as any other manager. You just have to make the right choices. I'm here to help, and between running the game and co-hosting the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast, I watch this stuff obsessively. If I get it wrong, well, we can all laugh about it later. It's a fantasy game, after all. This season, I'll publish three Fantasy tips articles every week -- one for each position -- as I expand my coverage even further. You'll get five recommendations for [guards], [forwards] and centers. The rest is up to you. It's time to talk about centers, so let's dive in. ### Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas (15.5 credits) [Jonas Valanciunas] is back in the EuroLeague after what feels like an eternity away. In the meantime, he grabbed more than 9,000 rebounds in the NBA. He arrives in Kaunas as Zalgiris's main offensive threat and should be a double-double machine, much like Arvydas Sabonis was in the 2003-04 season. ### Moses Wright, EA7 Emporio Armani Milan (14.0 credits) [Moses Wright] had an impressive season with Zalgiris and now arrives in Milan with a major role waiting for him. Expect efficient scoring, even from long range, blocked shots and plenty of rebounds. It's hard to choose between Valanciunas and Wright, so if your budget allows it, why not take both? ### Austin Wiley, FC Bayern Munich (11.0 credits) If you're looking for a slightly more affordable center, [Austin Wiley] could be your guy. He's coming off a fantastic BKT EuroCup season with Hapoel Bank Yahav Jerusalem, finishing as the competition's leading rebounder while averaging just 21 minutes per game. Yes, this is the EuroLeague, but his PIR floor looks remarkably solid. ### Allan Dokossi, Paris Basketball (8.0 credits) [Allan Dokossi] had his ups and downs last season while splitting time between power forward and center, but this year could bring much greater consistency. He's an excellent rebounder, an energy player and someone who fills the stat sheet. His first official game offered plenty of encouragement: 14 points and a PIR of 24 in just 22 minutes. ### Kevarrius Hayes, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (7.3 credits) There aren't many budget-friendly options at center, and several low-cost picks may struggle for meaningful playing time. Partizan has excellent depth in the paint, but [Kevarrius Hayes] is an experienced player, an elite shot-blocker and a strong rebounder available at an affordable price. He should definitely be on your radar.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Forwards
articles.text: The 2026-27 EuroLeague season is here, and so is the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. The game returns to a single-stage format in which every game matters, just like on the court. This season, I'm expanding my coverage with three Fantasy tips articles every week, one for each position -- [guards], forwards and [centers]. And yes, I'll revisit my previous picks every week, so I'll have to live with my successes and mistakes, the same way I do every week as co-host of the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast. It's time to talk about forwards. I'll stay away from fantasy king Sasha Vezenkov of Olympiacos Piraeus for obvious reasons and focus instead on players across a range of price points who can help your team succeed. Here are five forwards I like, other than Sasha. ### Jordan Nwora, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade (13.0 credits) This is an easy pick. [Jordan Nwora] is coming off a breakout season and now has arguably even more talent around him. Under Ibon Navarro, whose teams thrive in an up-tempo system, he could take another step forward. If Zvezda wins enough games, don't be surprised to see Nwora competing for MVP of the Round honors and All-EuroLeague Team recognition. ### Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Real Madrid (12.8 credits) [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot] was arguably one of the most consistent Fantasy performers last season with Baskonia. He joins a bigger club, but his role should remain largely the same: finding open spaces, knocking down shots and contributing efficiently across the board. His game looks perfectly suited to coach Pedro Martinez's system. ### Joel Parra, FC Barcelona (7.0 credits) Barcelona added plenty of new faces during the summer, so it's reasonable to expect the team's established players to log more minutes early in the season. [Joel Parra] is coming off an excellent preseason in which he regularly posted double-digit PIR performances. His attractive price tag only adds to the appeal. He looks ready for a breakout year. ### Eleftherios Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (4.5 credits) This might be one of the biggest surprises of the preseason. With Nigel Hayes-Davis sidelined, many expected Dinos Mitoglou and Juancho Hernangomez to absorb most of the extra minutes. Instead, [Eleftherios Mantzoukas] has been given a real opportunity and made the most of it throughout the preseason. If his three-point shot continues to fall, his Fantasy value could rise quickly. ### Stefan Joksimovic, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (4.0 credits) It's time for EuroLeague fans to get acquainted with [Stefan Joksimovic], who has starred at youth level for both Baskonia and the Slovenian national team. He's a gifted scorer and an all-around contributor who appears set to earn minutes right away. At the minimum Fantasy price, he represents one of the most intriguing budget options available.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Guards
articles.text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] is just around the corner, and I have some good news for you. I'm expanding my coverage, and from now on, you'll get three fantasy tips articles every week -- one each for guards, [forwards] and [centers]. As always, I'll also revisit my previous recommendations and hold myself accountable for the good picks and the bad ones. Since it's Round 1, however, there's no need to look back yet. No mistakes to regret and no victories to celebrate. I'm starting with guards, and I've included players from a variety of price ranges to help every Fantasy Challenge manager. Here are five guards who deserve serious consideration before tipoff. ### TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket (14.9 credits) One official game was enough to show what [TJ Shorts] can do as the leader of a team whose style fits him perfectly. He finished with 17 points, 6 rebounds, 7 assists and a PIR of 29 against FC Barcelona in the Spanish Super Cup. The signs are already there. Expect a big season. ### Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.8 credits) This one feels like a no-brainer. [Sylvain Francisco] earned All-EuroLeague First Team honors with Zalgiris last season and now joins a team whose primary scoring guard, Kendrick Nunn, is sidelined. Panathinaikos will play seven of its first eight games at home, giving Francisco an excellent opportunity to start the season strongly. ### Nigel Williams-Goss, Zalgiris Kaunas (9.7 credits) With Francisco no longer in Kaunas, [Nigel Williams-Goss] is expected to take on greater offensive responsibility and spend more time with the ball in his hands. He enjoyed a strong preseason and posted a PIR of 15 in his first official game despite playing only 16 minutes. Fantasy managers should keep a close eye on him, as his role is set to grow. ### Matteo Spagnolo, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (6.4 credits) It's true that injuries and absences during the preseason helped create opportunities for [Matteo Spagnolo], but the potential is hard to ignore. At just 6.4 credits, few players offer his upside. He recorded 10 points and 8 rebounds in his first official game of the season while playing nearly 22 minutes. That's outstanding value. ### Mario Saint-Supery, Valencia Basket (4.7 credits) [Mario Saint-Supery] left the NCAA to take on a significant role with Valencia and immediately showed why. Against Barcelona, he played a little over 18 minutes and produced 6 points, 4 assists and a PIR of 10. He's creative, versatile and capable of scoring in different ways. At under 5 credits, he may be the biggest bargain among guards heading into Round 1.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge: Reacting to the 10 most-bought players
articles.text: We are only days away from a new edition of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. It feels like yesterday when we created the game back in 2004. That means we're now entering the 23rd edition, and the Fantasy Challenge is more popular than ever. It's safe to say the game has developed a bit of a basketball cult following over the years, which is fantastic. We're one big Fantasy Challenge family. That makes me incredibly proud, so thank you, Fantasy managers. One of my favorite things about the start of the season is how unpredictable it can be. Some players I expect to dominate fail spectacularly, while some of the picks I dismiss end up becoming Fantasy gold. That gave me an idea: why not look at the Top 10 most-bought players and give my honest opinion on each one? Let's play this game. I'll go from least-owned to most-owned, all the way up to whoever's No. 1, and I haven't seen the list, honest to God. I'll simply be given a player's name, their ownership percentage, and asked to react. If you follow the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast, you already know my stance: if Sasha Vezenkov isn't No. 1, someone out there is making a mistake. ### 10. Mario Saint-Supery, Valencia Basket (4.7 credits, owned by 14.9%) This makes perfect sense. [Mario Saint-Supery] is very affordable, is expected to play significant minutes and should increase in value right away. He's in all of my teams, so I'm certainly not surprised to see him here. Good move, everyone. ### 9. Jean Montero, Olympiacos Piraeus (12.8 credits, owned by 15.0%) I don't love this pick. [Jean Montero] will probably need some time to settle in and play his best basketball. Last season, he struggled early, making just 14 of 46 shots over his first five games. I think it's a little too soon. ### 8. Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.8 credits, owned by 16.0%) This feels like a very straightforward pick. [Sylvain Francisco] was one of the best players in the 2025-26 EuroLeague, Kendrick Nunn is injured, and he's expected to take on a bigger role right away. A very solid choice. ### 7. Alec Peters, Olimpia Armani Milan (11.7 credits, owned by 17.2%) I understand why Fantasy managers are going for [Alec Peters]. He's an elite power forward at a very reasonable price, offers significant upside and is expected to enjoy an expanded role. Personally, I'd like to wait a little longer and see how quickly he adjusts to his new surroundings. ### 6. Ousmane Diop, Olimpia Armani Milan (4.0 credits, owned by 17.6%) Now this is a surprise. I hadn't even considered him. There are very few budget options at center this season, and [Ousmane Diop] is expected to get some minutes. My advice? Spend big on both center spots. It's one of the most important decisions Fantasy managers will make this year. ### 5. Jordan Nwora, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade (13.0 credits, owned by 17.6%) This is one of the names I expected to see. [Jordan Nwora] is a natural mismatch, right in the middle of his prime and playing for a coach whose style suits him perfectly. Let's just say he'll be in more than a few of my teams, and pretty often at that. ### 4. Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas (15.5 credits, owned by 25.8%) Probably the most important player in the game right now. If [Jonas Valanciunas] performs as expected, he'll be a double-double machine and an absolute must-have. As things stand, going without him feels very risky. He has a really high fantasy floor. ### 3. Arijan Lakic, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (4.0 credits, owned by 27.4%) I expected to see budget options this high on the list, but not [Arijan Lakic], to be honest. Yes, he should have a place in Partizan's rotation, but if you're shopping in this price range, I'd rather go with Stefan Joksimovic of Baskonia or Eleftherios Mantzoukas of Panathinaikos. ### 2. Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (13.6 credits, owned by 27.9%) One of my favorite guards in the game. It's difficult to choose [Carlik Jones] over Sylvain Francisco or TJ Shorts, but as the leader of his team with a home opener ahead of him, I completely understand this pick. He should deliver. ### 1. Sasha Vezenkov, Olympiacos Piraeus (17.0 credits, owned by 37.1%) [Sasha Vezenkov] bails you out. That's the bottom line. He rescues Fantasy managers from disaster, round after round. He's always there, whether you need a reliable captain in Round 1 or someone to save your score in Round 2. The Fantasy GOAT. Always has been. Maybe always will be.

articles.text: Preparations for the new season are in full swing, and Basketball Sphere is set to deliver the most comprehensive EuroLeague Fantasy coverage throughout the entire 2026/27 campaign. We will systematically cover every critical angle for your draft and weekly lineups. Through these deep dives, you will gain key insights into coaching tactics and rotation roles – the crucial factors that drive Fantasy output. Choosing a coach in fantasy is often underestimated, even though coaches can deliver a large number of points for a very low number of credits. It is extremely rare for a player who costs, say, 5-6 credits to score 20 fantasy points, while this is a very common occurrence with coaches. Therefore, our advice is to never save credits when choosing a coach and, if possible, look to keep the same coach for several upcoming rounds in order to save transfers for players and improve your team. In the following article, we will take a look at 20 EuroLeague coaches for this season and answer the questions of whether they are good options and whether you should select coaches from the opposing team when they play against them. EuroLeague Fantasy Basketball Sphere Competiton: JOIN the Challenge and Win Prizes 1. Zeljko Obradovic – Panathinaikos – 10.0 credits Zeljko Obradovic stands as the most expensive head coach option in EuroLeague Fantasy, making him the safest anchor for fantasy rosters throughout the season. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Produce Well but Aren’t Fantasy Options
articles.text: Preparations for the new season are in full swing, and Basketball Sphere is set to deliver the most comprehensive EuroLeague Fantasy coverage throughout the entire 2026/27 campaign. Our goal is to provide you with all the data and insights needed to build a championship-caliber team and make smart decisions round after round. Alongside our team-by-team breakdowns, each day will bring a new dedicated topic to keep you ahead of the competition. We will systematically cover every critical angle for your draft and weekly lineups. Through these deep dives, you will gain key insights into coaching tactics and rotation roles – the crucial factors that drive Fantasy output. There are players who are capable of completely changing the pace of a game and scoring a large number of points in a very short period of time, but that doesn’t translate into a strong Fantasy performance. This is simply due to the high number of negative stats they accumulate, such as missed shots, shots blocked, turnovers, fouls committed and so on. This is often a characteristic of good scorers, because if they don’t score a lot of points, it is difficult for them to post a high Fantasy score. These are what we call Fantasy traps, and more experienced players have been avoiding them for years. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Difficulty of the schedule in the first five rounds 1. Kendrick Nunn – Guard – 14.6 credits Kendrick Nunn is the prime example of a player whose strong real-life performances rarely translate into high Fantasy output. Towards the end of last season, even a 20-point scoring night could leave him with a single-digit EuroLeague Fantasy score. His main valuation killer is efficiency. Nunn frequently accumulates high foul counts while drawing very few himself. Additionally, his Fantasy baseline takes heavy hits from a high volume of turnovers and blocked shots. While Nunn will inevitably post solid scoring numbers , his high turnover rate, defensive fouls, and shot selection limit his Fantasy floor. Within a deep, crowded Panathinaikos roster , he carries far too much risk to justify a steep 14.6 credit price tag. Avoid him for your fantasy roster and look for more complete stat-sheet fillers. EuroLeague Preview: The toughest stretch on every team’s schedule 2. Kevin Punter – Guard – 13.6 credits Barcelona’s new captain is another high-profile name to approach with caution. Unlike Kendrick Nunn , foul trouble is not Kevin Punter’s main drawback. Instead, his Fantasy limitation comes down to a lack of peripheral stats . For a guard who regularly sees around 27 minutes of playing time per game, Punter produces surprisingly low rebound and assist totals. Across his EuroLeague career, he has averaged a modest 2.0 rebounds and 2.3 assists. Because his Fantasy production relies almost entirely on point scoring and fouls drawn, any cold shooting night results in a severely low score. Punter will certainly have explosive scoring games , but without consistent contributions in secondary categories, it is difficult to justify spending 13.6 credits on him for your Fantasy lineup. Target guards who offer a higher baseline through playmaking or glass-cleaning instead. The EuroLeague Regression Candidates: Who Is Unlikely to Repeat Last Season? 3. Dwayne Bacon – Forward – 12.7 credits Dwayne Bacon steps into the classic NBA-style sixth man role for Dubai . The moment he touches the floor, his primary duty is to generate instant offense, capable of firing off a massive volume of shots in very short stretches. The downside to this high-usage style is poor shot selection. Bacon frequently settles for tough, contested attempts, leading to a high frequency of missed field goals and blocked shots. In EuroLeague Fantasy, these efficiency penalties heavily eat into his total score. Because his value hinges almost exclusively on raw volume , Bacon requires a near-flawless shooting night just to sniff a PIR of 20. At a premium cost of 12.7 credits, his volatile fantasy floor makes him a huge gamble. Look elsewhere for forwards with more reliable multi-category production. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: 20+ Minute Players Who Don’t Cost Much 4. Patty Mills – Guard – 12.3 credits Patty Mills enters his debut EuroLeague campaign with Asvel, but his Fantasy prospects look grim. Asvel is projected to struggle near the bottom of the standings again, often playing from behind – an unfavorable environment for a rhythm-dependent veteran. Mills relies almost entirely on perimeter scoring to drive his Fantasy numbers. He offers minimal impact in secondary categories like rebounding, defensive stocks, or elite playmaking. Without those baseline contributions, achieving a top-tier PIR requires an exceptionally hot shooting night from beyond the arc . On a team that will frequently face tough defensive pressure and uphill game scripts, banking on high-efficiency shooting nights is a dangerous strategy. At 12.3 credits, Mills carries immense risk and profiles as one of the biggest fantasy traps on the market entering the season. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Young Players to Watch for the New Season 5. Jared Butler – Guard – 10.1 credits Including Jared Butler on this list was a close call. With his initial EuroLeague adjustment period now behind him, he has the talent to deliver a true breakout campaign and comfortably outperform last year’s numbers. However, if he reproduces last season’s habits, he remains a dangerous Fantasy trap . Butler frequently picked up unnecessary personal fouls, committed costly turnovers, and avoided heavy physical contact, resulting in very few fouls drawn. These negative plays systematically drag down his PIR baseline, regardless of his scoring output. If Butler cleans up those mistakes and takes command of his role, he could easily transform from a high-risk trap into one of the biggest Fantasy steals of the season at an affordable 10.1 credits. But until he proves that shift on the floor, tread carefully.
